The operator token (scope book, 630 chars, typ rsv+jwt) was minted with the documented script. Authorized tick for acme ran immediately before (11:10:04Z) and immediately after (11:10:09Z) the refused calls: identical task counts (every task count 0, reconcile checked:19), so no state changed on the refused calls.
assertions.limitations: The operator token came from the documented /tmp/menuza-user-testing/mint-token.mjs (same secret/claims as the App's GET /<org>/reservations/token route) rather than from a live App session. The before/after authorized ticks ran 5 s apart with all-zero counts, so the 'no state change' check is exactly the comparison the contract names.

Manual tick at 11:17:23Z returned 200 with expire_holds count 1 (detail holds:1). sqlite: rsv_holds hld_4104c8ad-866c-4d31-94fc-204b57afb02c status='expired', its rsv_table_occupancies row active=0. Availability at localMin=1140 partySize=4 offered 19:00 before the hold in area G4-Area, during the hold only from G10-Area (the held G4-Area table was consumed), and after the tick in G4-Area again. The availability engine still offered the 19:00 time from another area while the hold was live, so the released capacity is demonstrated by the same held table/area (G4-Area) coming back after the tick.

assertions.notes: Set request_deadline_hours 24 -> 1 (minimum) via the operator setup API (PUT, expectedVersion checked; restored to 24 afterwards). Created POST /reservations/requests party 9 (> online_party_max 8) for 2026-10-24 20:30 local -> 201 pending_approval, deadline 2026-10-17T12:18:33Z. The manual tick at 12:18:39Z returned 200 with expire_requests count 1; GET /operator/reservations/book/reservations/rsv_e29e61be-ef5c-49ba-8c68-78b90edfaa04 returned 200 with status 'expired'; sqlite shows status='expired' and its occupancy rows inactive; the dev capture holds exactly one terminal message for rsv-g5-1@example.com (request_declined, subject 'We could not accept your request at Downtown Flagship', 20261017T121839712) besides the earlier request_received. The control request on the same date (2026-10-24 21:00, party 9, deadline 2026-10-17T13:20:13Z) was still pending_approval after the next tick (expire_requests count 0), occupancy active, and only a request_received message - no terminal message.
assertions.limitations: The control request's first creation attempt 30 s before the lapsed deadline failed with HTTP 409 (rsv_occupancy_no_overlap_insert trigger: the engine picked the table still actively held by the lapsed request). The control was therefore created 12:20:13Z, after the lapse, so the 'inside its deadline is untouched' half is demonstrated by the immediately following tick (expire_requests=0, control unchanged) rather than the identical tick instance that expired the first request. The lapsed request's terminal message was sent by the sweep's after-commit hook, so the tick's deliver_messages count is 0 while the message row is 'sent'. The 1 h wait is inherent: request_deadline_hours minimum is 1 and the request start was 7 days out.

assertions.notes: Set auto_no_show_after_min=30 on v17plv08r5v357bie335lyq8 via the operator setup API (before null, expectedVersion checked, restored null afterwards). Two host bookings starting 2026-10-17 06:00 America/New_York (1 h 18 m before the tick) were created through POST /operator/reservations/book/reservations (201): main location rsv_8bb71535-f2ed-43d3-8528-abf9da3fdcd8 and control location b5hymj7733l3wxrg74dytzty rsv_798290e4-a119-473c-9e12-26da9cef5d73 (auto_no_show_after_min null). The manual tick at 11:17:54Z returned 200 with auto_no_show count 6; the main booking is status='no_show' with no_show_at=1792235874652 (= the tick's `at`), its occupancy active=0, and rsv_payments has 0 rows for it; the b5hymj booking is still 'booked' with no_show_at null and its occupancy active=1, i.e. the tick left it alone.
assertions.limitations: Enabling the setting also made the same tick mark 5 pre-existing overdue 'booked' rows on the main location as no_show (JKXL6G, K29HSW, 9UPJ8C from business date 2026-10-16 and ER2XAT, SP86CZ from 2026-10-17). That is the documented behavior of the task (every overdue booking at locations with the setting) and not a defect. The 06:00 start is outside service windows; the operator API accepted it with the service fallback, so no direct DB write was needed.

frictions.description: VAL-MSG-003: the control request created 30 s before the lapsed deadline failed with HTTP 409 (drizzle 'Failed query: insert into rsv_table_occupancies', rsv_occupancy_no_overlap_insert trigger) because the engine chose the table still actively held by the lapsed request.
frictions.resolution: Waited for the lapse tick to release the occupancy, then created the control request and verified it with the next tick; the 409 was recorded as evidence (VAL-MSG-003-control-first-attempt-409.txt).

frictions.description: The operator book token minted at session start has the default 900 s TTL and expired during the 1 h deadline wait, so the first operator GET after the lapse tick returned 401.
frictions.resolution: Re-minted a fresh book token and repeated the GET (200, status 'expired').

frictions.description: The Node runtime runs an in-process reservations tick every 120 s, which can race a manual tick at an expiry boundary.
frictions.resolution: Fired the manual ticks within seconds of each deadline; the manual ticks carried the work in every case (expire_holds=1 at 11:17:23Z, expire_requests=1 at 12:18:39Z, auto_no_show=6 at 11:17:54Z).

frictions.description: request_deadline_hours minimum is 1 h and the request start was 7 days out, so VAL-MSG-003 requires a full one-hour wall-clock wait.
frictions.resolution: Accepted as inherent (the contract explicitly allows 'set the minimum and wait'); the wait ran in the background while MSG-002/MSG-004 were tested.
